A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MRRE study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching content across table and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual benchmark evaluations, vector ablations, cross-modal transfer experiments, translation checks, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparator results in Tables 1–2 and inference-latency measurements in Table 6.

M1.justification: The reasoning-enhancement vectors, output-anchoring vectors, normalization, and sequential inference interventions in Sections 3.2–3.4 are unchanged. The debiasing variant is also retained. The new LC algorithm documents evaluation rather than changing MRRE.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MGSM, MSVAMP, MMathVerse, and MMathVista with English and the same eight non-English languages. The represented reasoning tasks and visual task categories remain unchanged; the added comparator results use existing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add Few-Shot, SFT, and Multilingual-CoT comparisons for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. This substantially broadens the corresponding comparisons beyond the unmodified models and Language forcing to include additional prompting and fine-tuning approaches. Comparators for the other four models remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Section 5.6 evaluates Qwen2.5-7B latency on a single NVIDIA A100 using time to first token and time per output token. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Appendix D newly documents LC implementation without establishing that the earlier evaluation procedure changed.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 adds an efficiency analysis testing inference overhead, supported by Table 6. Existing intervention visualizations, cross-modal transfer tests, English-debiasing experiments, component and hyperparameter ablations, and Appendix C case studies are retained.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance testing. New comparator and latency results are point estimates. FastText confidence thresholds in Appendix D concern language classification rather than uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 substantially expand results with three additional comparators, while matched pre-existing scores remain unchanged. For example, the new Few-Shot result on Swahili MMathVista is 34.8% versus MRRE's retained 28.6% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B. New Table 6 reports base/MRRE latencies of 83.7/84.1 ms for first-token generation and 32.1/32.5 ms per output token.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the Transformer formulation, and the mathematical vector constructions are unchanged. Appendix D supplies operational pseudocode for the existing LC metric; it adds no theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free representation-engineering contribution and generalization claims. The headline improvements of 5.48%, 7.54% for low-resource languages, and 3.78% in language consistency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.6 newly characterizes offline preparation as a negligible one-time cost and interprets the measured latency overhead as preserving fast generation and practical deployability. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations concerning internal-model access and restricted experimental coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix D specifies LC preprocessing, sentence decomposition, FastText confidence of at least 0.8, and a target-language character share above 80%. The latency experiment also identifies its hardware. Conversely, v2 removes the main-text description of forward translation using Google Translate v2 and human checking; Appendix A retains the back-translation procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Barua et al. (2025), Qin et al. (2023, 2025), Xiao et al. (2026), and Zhao et al. (2025), supporting the new comparator and existing multilingual-reasoning discussion. The overall positioning and claimed novelty remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical corrections, condenses benchmark descriptions, adds baseline and efficiency discussion, and inserts the LC appendix. It also revises the author block, adds acknowledgements, and moves Usage of LLMs from Appendix D to E. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain comparator rows, and the Qwen2.5-VL block is reordered in Table 1. v2 adds latency Table 6 and Algorithm 1, renumbers later tables, and adjusts surrounding layout. Existing figures and case-study displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens comparative evaluation through additional baselines, makes LC scoring more reproducible, and supplies measured inference overhead. These are useful improvements to the unchanged core study. Their benefit is limited by unspecified configurations for the new baselines, timing evidence from only one model and hardware setting, and the loss of forward-translation and human-checking documentation.
